guides.title: How to Collect Family Recipes at the Reunion — While Everyone's at One Table
guides.description: The family reunion is the one day the whole recipe archive is alive in one backyard. A gentle plan for collecting the dishes, the stories, and the voices — between the spades game and the second plate.

guides.title: How to Digitize Handwritten Recipe Cards (Without Losing the Handwriting)
guides.description: A step-by-step guide to digitizing handwritten recipe cards: photograph them right, transcribe them fast, and keep the handwriting as part of the heirloom.

guides.title: How to Make a Family Cookbook Everyone Actually Uses
guides.description: From shoebox to heirloom: how to collect the recipes, gather the stories, get the whole family contributing, and print a family cookbook worth passing down.

guides.title: How to Preserve Family Recipes — Before They're Lost
guides.description: A practical 5-step method for preserving family recipes: capture the dish, the story, and the voice of the person who makes it — before it's too late.

guides.title: 25 Questions to Ask the Family Cook (While You Still Can)
guides.description: 25 questions that turn a recipe interview into a family memory — about the dish, the hands that made it, and the tables it fed. Bring a recorder.

guides.title: "Until It Looks Right": Preserving Recipes That Have No Measurements
guides.description: A pinch, a feel, until it looks like Louisiana — how to preserve family recipes that were never measured, from cooks who carry them by hand and by heart.

guides.title: Record Family Recipes in Their Own Voice — Before It's Too Late
guides.description: Why a 60-second voice recording preserves more of a family recipe than any written card — and how to run a 10-minute recording session with the cook you love.
